thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xxs for prompt-router-v3-experiment (route: /v1/prompt/edge) — error rate >= 8% over 3m, latency P95 up 2.2x
pagerduty: Paging oncall-sre — urgent
oncall-sre: I got the page, looking now. joining the thread
alice.k: seeing 502s at edge-proxy and increased KV cache misses. Canary hosts for r-2026-04-12-19 show cpu throttling and retry storms
ben.p: logs show a new config landed in the rollout: ff key ff.prompt_routing_experimental_v3 -> true for 15% traffic
mike.s: confirmed, rollout id r-2026-04-12-19 pushed 18:02 UTC, canary slice 15%
oncall-sre: @deploy-bot can you pause/kill the FF? we need to evacuate canary to stable router
deploy-bot: Received command: toggle_flag(ff.prompt_routing_experimental_v3,false) — executing...
deploy-bot: OK — flag toggled to false for all traffic (propagation in progress) 
oncall-sre: running quick check: curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.dev/v1/prompt -H 'x-route: edge' | head -n 1
oncall-sre: edge now returning 200s in initial probes, but some lingering inflight 502s observed
alice.k: telemetry shows error_rate dropping from 8.4% -> 1.1% over last 60s, p95 latency trending down
ben.p: we also disabled a new rate-limiter rule that was added in the same deploy; it was blocking downstream KV connections
mike.s: can we confirm no customer-facing timeouts? cust-eng, any reports?
cust-eng: one customer on the bridge reported degraded completions ~18:15 UTC, but they were auto-retried and we notified them. No broad CSAT alerts yet. Preparing a short status note for affected customers
oncall-sre: spinning up extra canary-stable proxies to drain inflight connections: kubectl scale deploy/prompt-proxy-stable --replicas=6
oncall-sre: also forcing canary abort: /ops/deploy rollback r-2026-04-12-19 --force
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated, job id jb-8932, progress: 3/3 services rolled back
alice.k: telemetry looks good after rollback + flag kill. Error rate back to baseline 0.2%. Will keep observing for 15m
ben.p: note to team: root cause looks like a combination of experimental routing change + new local rate-limiter interacting poorly with KV cache under moderate load
oncall-sre: handing off to next oncall: @mike.s you'll own the 15m observation window and customer follow-up, I’ll update the incident ticket and clear the page if stable
mike.s: ack, taking over. I'll post a short customer-facing blurb and add postmortem owners
cust-eng: drafting message: "We briefly routed a portion of traffic to an experimental prompt routing pathway which caused elevated errors for a small subset of requests. We have disabled the experiment and rolled back the deploy. Service is stable; we will follow up with a detailed timeline." feedback?
oncall-sre: small nit: include impacted window 18:02-18:18 UTC and that retries were automatic
cust-eng: updated and will send once green.
oncall-sre: added tags: severity=sev2, mitigated=true, mitigation=flag_kill+rollback, mitigator=oncall-sre
ben.p: capturing commands for postmortem: toggle_flag(...), kubectl scale, /ops/deploy rollback r-2026-04-12-19, and disabled rate-limiter config id rl-449
oncall-sre: leaving the thread, @mike.s you have handoff. ping me if it surfaces again. :thumbsup:
mike.s: thanks team. will monitor metrics (errors, p95, kv_miss_rate) and sync in 10m then update ticket.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: page resolved (status=mitigated) — followup required: postmortem and customer communication.
